name: TE Connectivity
key_signal: TEL trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages after a 16.6% three-month drawdown, yet MACD has just turned positive and shares sit almost exactly at the 50-day SMA, suggesting a tentative base is forming.
thesis: TEL's fundamentals remain solid for a name that's sold off from its $252 high to ~$204: 14.5% revenue growth, 20.3% operating margins, 22.7% ROE, and a forward P/E of just 16.2x versus a 20.9x trailing multiple implies the market expects meaningful earnings acceleration. Free cash flow of $2.3B on $18.7B revenue and a moderate 43.8x debt-to-equity give balance-sheet flexibility to keep buying back stock and paying its 1.47% dividend through a cyclical soft patch. The recent uptick in MACD histogram and a steadying RSI near 52 (neutral, not oversold-to-death) hint the worst of the momentum washout may be behind it, and with 20 analysts still carrying a consensus 'buy,' there's a constituency ready to defend the stock on any earnings beat.
bear_case: The technical picture is genuinely broken, not just noisy: TEL is below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages (no golden cross), down 16.6% over three months and nearly 15% over six months, with 33% annualized volatility signaling the market is actively repricing risk, not just consolidating. TE Connectivle's end markets (auto, industrial, sensors) are exposed to a global manufacturing slowdown and tariff-driven input cost pressure, which could explain why forward estimates already discount earnings growth the stock hasn't yet delivered — if that growth disappoints, the 'cheap forward multiple' argument evaporates and the stock reverts toward its 52-week low of $177 rather than back to its high of $252. A beta of 1.17 also means any broader market drawdown amplifies TEL's downside just as this bounce is trying to take hold.
